from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 7  # sources
    J = 5  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [237, 243, 246, 135, 178, 212, 142]
    demands = [44, 20, 43, 52, 20]
    cost_matrix = [[26.02, 29.07, 22.13, 17.71, 21.03], [5.2, 16.04, 11.43, 7.01, 13.65], [22.2, 15.8, 15.03, 24.52, 9.82], [16.09, 9.63, 29.97, 8.74, 29.55], [3.27, 16.51, 28.17, 3.69, 13.85], [4.03, 23.16, 24.41, 18.11, 6.07], [15.1, 7.72, 25.44, 6.04, 27.12]]
    emission_matrix = [[1.0, 2.5, 2.79, 14.76, 7.24], [3.73, 12.09, 7.28, 16.65, 3.07], [7.46, 7.37, 16.02, 8.62, 9.93], [12.37, 6.55, 10.06, 12.93, 13.16], [20.0, 11.25, 14.44, 17.89, 15.54], [14.92, 9.3, 10.1, 17.63, 5.77], [9.63, 8.21, 10.68, 10.61, 15.54]]
    fixed_costs = [[59, 155, 230, 224, 72], [256, 110, 149, 256, 84], [192, 90, 262, 181, 125], [175, 279, 203, 190, 232], [107, 124, 149, 119, 233], [78, 236, 209, 296, 286], [72, 142, 275, 280, 189]]
    moq = [[16, 16, 19, 14, 14], [8, 8, 12, 19, 12], [17, 5, 7, 5, 15], [14, 7, 15, 6, 15], [7, 5, 16, 12, 6], [12, 11, 17, 15, 6], [11, 9, 8, 15, 14]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: VP, Supply Chain
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director

Subject: Balancing shipping cost and carbon across our warehouse-to-store network

Context
We are preparing our next-phase shipping plan across our warehouse and store network with a clear need to balance financial discipline and our sustainability commitments. Every lane in our network carries both a per‑unit shipping expense and a per‑unit carbon footprint. In practice, lanes with the lowest freight expense often produce higher emissions, while cleaner options tend to come at a premium. Our approach must transparently quantify these trade‑offs and deliver a plan that meets service requirements without compromising our environmental targets.

Operational rules we must respect
- Route activation costs: Enabling any lane requires a fixed setup outlay (e.g., contract fees, customs, dock readiness). A lane is either enabled or not; if enabled, the setup charge applies regardless of how much we ship on it.
- Minimum order quantities: Once a lane is enabled, we must ship at least a predetermined threshold on that lane to justify handling time and equipment utilization. Partial loads below this threshold are not accepted.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can receive from only a limited number of warehouses due to receiving capacity, vendor management effort, and contractual boundaries. This pushes us to consolidate inbound flows.

Capacity and service expectations
- Warehouses have finite inventory available for outbound shipments, and outbound allocations cannot exceed those supplies.
- Stores have minimum demand requirements that must be fulfilled within the planning horizon.
- Any enabled lane must carry at least its minimum order, and each store must be served by no more than its allowed number of supplying warehouses.

Management priority
Leadership has set relative importance weights for cost and emissions to guide trade‑offs. In our evaluation, per‑unit shipping expenses and per‑unit emissions will be combined using these weights so that each lane’s variable impacts are comparable on a single blended basis. In addition, every enabled lane contributes its full setup charge to the total—these setup charges are added in full and are not scaled by the cost or emissions weights. This construct ensures we do not hide fixed enablement costs inside the weighting scheme.

Goal
Select which lanes to enable and determine shipment volumes on each such that:
- Warehouse supplies are not exceeded and store demands are met,
- Any enabled lane moves at least its minimum order quantity,
- Each store is served by no more than its allowed number of warehouses,
- And the combined total—weighted variable shipping expense, weighted emissions, plus full setup charges—is as low as practicable given our priorities and operational rules.

This approach will yield a practical shipment plan that respects real receiving capacity and logistics realities while making the trade‑offs between cost and sustainability explicit for leadership review.
